newsitem.title: FRANCE: French trawlers head for forbidden Guernsey zone.
newsitem.headline: French trawlers head for forbidden Guernsey zone.

text.p: French trawlers approached a contested patch of water off the Channel island of Guernsey on Monday in a showdown over fishing rights, but French and British officials predicted their protest would be peaceful.
"I imagine they'll just go round in a little circle until they get fed up," said a spokeswoman at the British embassy in Paris. "We understand it's just a demonstration."

The French trawler skippers, who will be accompanied by the unarmed civilian surveillance vessel Coriandre, are angry about Britain's decision to go back on a 1994 agreement granting them fishing rights in a patch of water southeast of Guernsey called the Sark Box.
Some 25 to 30 French fishing boats and the Coriandre were expected to expected to arrive off Guernsey shortly after 3 p.m. (1400 GMT), French maritime authorities said.

"We do not want French fishing vessels to be prevented from entering this zone," a French Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters. "While we await the resumption of negotiations, expected in January, we want the status quo to be maintained."
Maritime authorities said weather was very bad in the area, with 14-foot (four-metre) waves likely to prevent any fishing.

Britain's decision to end the 1994 agreement was made last month, but Sunday was the first day that Guernsey authorities had said they would enforce the move by prosecuting French boats which entered the contested area.

The British embassy spokeswoman said that following diplomatic contacts at the weekend between French and British authorities, it was agreed that the French fishermen would be allowed to enter the area without incident so they could demonstrate their anger.
"Both sides agree that the last thing we want is any incidents. Both sides would like negotiations to resume as soon as possible," she said.
Guernsey authorities have already set out proposals for a new accord to replace the 1994 agreement, and the French have made counter-proposals, she said.
"We now hope for early talks on a replacement regime," she said.
The 1994 agreement allowed French trawlers to operate in the island's waters in return for rights for Guernsey fishermen to fish in French waters.

French diplomatic sources said the French authorities were determined to retain fishing rights in the contested area and had displayed their commitment by despatching the Coriandre to accompany the trawlers.
